# Design document (M2) -- Don't Look Behind You (Jackson Stokes, Gage Boullosa)

Hardware and pin map: [docs/HARDWARE.md](docs/HARDWARE.md). Problem statement: [PROBLEM.md](PROBLEM.md).

## 1. Architecture

![Architecture: processes, kernel components, hardware, and the rate on every link](docs/architecture.svg)

Seven processes on the Pi 5, all started and watched by `dlby-super`. Sensor data goes
straight from the capture processes to `fuse-hub`, which decides the alert state and
forwards a copy of everything to `store`. Unlike a sampler → storage → analysis pipeline,
storage is deliberately off the alert path, so a slow SD write can never delay an alert.

### Processes
| Process | Owner | Role | Scheduling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dlby-super` | shared | fork/exec every child, `waitpid`, restart with backoff, kill a child that misses heartbeats for 5 s | SCHED_FIFO 90, asleep almost always |
| `cap-radar` | Gage | read `/dev/ttyAMA2`, frame-sync, parse targets, timestamp each frame | SCHED_FIFO 60 |
| `cap-sonar` | Gage | trigger GPIO23 on an absolute 60 ms deadline; read kernel-timestamped echo edges on GPIO24 from the gpio character device | SCHED_FIFO 60 |
| `fuse-hub` | Jackson | CLEAR → APPROACHING → IN_ZONE → CLEAR state machine; ignores targets that aren't approaching | SCHED_FIFO 70 |
| `alert` | shared | drive the LED (GPIO17) and buzzer (GPIO22); show a fault pattern if `fuse-hub` goes silent | SCHED_FIFO 80 |
| `store` | Jackson | append-only log of raw samples and state changes that survives a power cut | SCHED_OTHER, nice +5 |
| `status-lcd` | shared | 1602 LCD over I2C1 for bench and demo only. Separate from `alert` so a slow I2C write can't delay the alert | SCHED_OTHER |

Kernel components used: the RP1 UART and tty layer (radar), the gpio character device
with edge events stamped on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (ultrasonic, LED, buzzer), `i2c-dev` on
I2C1 (LCD), and ext4 on the SD card (`store`). The product makes no network calls and has
no LAN interface in this milestone.

### IPC
Every process-to-process link is a Unix domain socket of type `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. Each
receiver (`fuse-hub`, `alert`, `store`, `status-lcd`) listens on `/run/dlby/<name>.sock`
(directory mode 0700). Senders connect and send with `MSG_NOSIGNAL`. On EOF, `EPIPE`, or a
failed connect (`ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the receiver is restarting), they reconnect
with backoff (50 ms doubling to 1 s), so any one process can restart without re-wiring the
others. `dlby-super` keeps a socketpair to each child for heartbeats only. We chose
seqpacket because it keeps message boundaries, a dead peer shows up immediately as
EOF/`EPOLLHUP`, and with `SOCK_CLOEXEC` fds can't leak across restarts. Our rates are a few
hundred bytes per second, so shared memory's speed isn't needed.

### Links and rates
| Link | Transport | Payload | Rate | Bandwidth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| radar → `cap-radar` | UART 115200 8N1 | frame = 10 B + payload | ~10 Hz | ≤1.3 KB/s (link capacity 11.5 KB/s) |
| `cap-sonar` → HC-SR04 | GPIO23 out | 10 µs trigger pulse | 16 Hz | — |
| HC-SR04 → `cap-sonar` | GPIO24 edge events | 2 edges per ping | 32 events/s | — |
| `cap-radar` → `fuse-hub` | UDS | `radar_msg` ~64 B (timestamp, seq, target count, targets) | 10 Hz | ~640 B/s |
| `cap-sonar` → `fuse-hub` | UDS | `sonar_msg` 24 B (timestamp, seq, cm or timeout) | 16 Hz | ~400 B/s |
| `fuse-hub` → `alert` | UDS | `alert_msg` 16 B (state, timestamp) | on change + 2 Hz keepalive | <50 B/s |
| `fuse-hub` → `store` | UDS | raw messages forwarded, plus state changes | ~26 Hz | ~1.1 KB/s (~4 MB/h, ~190 MB per 48 h soak) |
| `fuse-hub` → `status-lcd` | UDS | status snapshot ~64 B | 2 Hz | ~130 B/s |
| each child → `dlby-super` | UDS, one per child | heartbeat 8 B | 1 Hz | 8 B/s each |
| `status-lcd` → LCD | I2C1 at 100 kHz | 2×16 characters | 2 Hz | — |

Two numbers to confirm on hardware:
- **Ultrasonic rate.** 16 Hz, not the "~20 Hz" in HARDWARE.md. The HC-SR04 needs at least
  60 ms between pings so it doesn't hear the previous ping's echo, and the bench sketch
  already uses 60 ms.
- **Radar payload size** is an estimate until the LD2451 frame format is checked against
  the datasheet and real captures.

### Fusion states and driver signals
While both sensors are healthy, neither alone raises an alert: APPROACHING needs a radar
track, and IN_ZONE needs the ultrasonic to confirm it. If one sensor is lost, the survivor
still warns, but in a pattern the driver can tell apart. `fuse-hub` starts in BLIND. It
moves to the normal states once both sensors report, or to the matching DEG state if one
reports and the other stays silent past its loss timeout (radar 1 s, ultrasonic 8 pings).

The rule for the driver:
- **Solid:** warning, both sensors healthy.
- **1 Hz flash:** warning from one sensor only (unconfirmed).
- **Short blink every 2 s:** armed. A single blink means both sensors are healthy; a
  double blink means one sensor is lost.
- **4 Hz blink:** not protected.
- **Dark:** system not running.

The LED is never dark while the system is working, so dark can't be mistaken for "clear".
The buzzer is an active (fixed-tone) part, so its patterns are timing only.

| State | Meaning | LED | Buzzer | LCD (bench) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLEAR | both healthy, nothing near | single 50 ms blink every 2 s | silent | `ARMED` |
| APPROACHING | both healthy, radar track approaching | solid | silent | `APPROACH 23m` |
| IN_ZONE | both healthy, ultrasonic confirms the track | solid | 4 Hz beeps | `IN ZONE` |
| DEG_CLEAR | one sensor lost, survivor sees nothing | double blink every 2 s | one chirp on entry | `RADAR LOST` / `SONAR LOST` |
| DEG_APPROACHING | ultrasonic lost, radar track approaching | 1 Hz flash | silent | `SONAR LOST APPR` |
| DEG_IN_ZONE | radar lost, something at 0.2–4 m (unconfirmed) | 1 Hz flash | 1 Hz beeps | `RADAR LOST ZONE` |
| BLIND | both sensors lost, or hub just started | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, again every 30 s | `NO SENSORS` |
| HUB_LOST (`alert`'s own state) | no message from `fuse-hub` for 1 s | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, again every 30 s | `HUB DOWN` |
| no process running | supervisor restart, boot, power off | dark | silent | stale text |

BLIND and HUB_LOST share a pattern on purpose. Both mean "not protected", and the LCD
tells them apart on the bench.

## 2. Mechanism mapping

### C: SCHED_FIFO on the alert chain (`cap-radar`, `cap-sonar`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`)
**Not the justification: range accuracy.** The kernel timestamps echo edges in the GPIO
interrupt path, so the measured range, (t_fall − t_rise) × 343 m/s ÷ 2, doesn't depend on
when `cap-sonar` gets to run. The trigger time doesn't matter either, because the echo's
rising edge is the reference. Scheduling could only cost range data if the kernel's
16-event edge buffer overflowed, which takes more than about 250 ms of starvation at
32 events/s.

**The justification:**
1. **Alert latency under load.** A sensor reading reaches the buzzer through three
   wakeups: capture, `fuse-hub`, `alert`. Under the default scheduler, with `store`
   flushing to the SD card and other load on the CPU, each wakeup can slip by milliseconds
   to tens of milliseconds. At a 30 km/h closing speed (8.3 m/s), 50 ms is about 0.4 m of
   cyclist travel inside a 4 m zone. The whole chain runs SCHED_FIFO, with priority rising
   downstream (capture 60 < `fuse-hub` 70 < `alert` 80) so each stage runs as soon as its
   input arrives.
2. **Regular trigger period.** A late wakeup stretches the gap between pings, which adds
   directly to the worst-case detection delay. Periodic wakeups use absolute deadlines
   (`clock_nanosleep` with `TIMER_ABSTIME`) so lateness doesn't accumulate.
3. **Radar timestamps.** UART bytes are buffered by the kernel and timestamped in user
   space when read, so radar timestamps do shift with scheduling delay. The fusion check
   that the ultrasonic hit matches the radar's last track depends on them.

**Keeping C safe:** every real-time process calls `mlockall`. The kernel's real-time
throttle (`sched_rt_runtime_us`, 950 ms per second) stays at its default, so a real-time
child stuck in a loop can't starve the system. `dlby-super` has the highest priority and
almost always sleeps, so it can still detect and kill a stuck child.

### E: multi-process architecture with a supervisor
**Justification:** an outdoor sensor pod will fail in ordinary use (cable knocked loose,
water, a locked-up ultrasonic). The driver must keep getting warnings from whatever still
works, and must never read "LED dark" as "no cyclist". One process per job means one
failure costs one component, and a supervisor turns every failure into a visible state.

`dlby-super`:
- **Starts** every child in order (`store`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`, `status-lcd`, `cap-radar`,
  `cap-sonar`). Each gets a heartbeat socketpair and nothing else, since every fd is
  `O_CLOEXEC`/`SOCK_CLOEXEC`.
- **Detects crashes** with SIGCHLD through a `signalfd`, then reaps with `waitpid(WNOHANG)`.
- **Detects hangs.** Each child sends a heartbeat every 1 s from its main event loop, never
  from a side thread, so a stuck loop stops the heartbeat. After 5 s of silence super sends
  SIGTERM, and SIGKILL 500 ms later. Children get 10 s after start to send their first
  heartbeat (CLAUDE.md allows up to 60 s).
- **Restarts** with backoff from 100 ms doubling to 30 s, reset after 60 s healthy. It never
  gives up on a sensor, since it may be re-plugged.
- **Reads exit codes:** 0 means asked to stop (no restart). 69 `EX_UNAVAILABLE` (device
  missing) and 70 `EX_SOFTWARE` (internal error) mean restart with backoff. 78 `EX_CONFIG`
  means don't restart, and log it.
- **Clears stuck outputs.** A killed `alert` can't turn its GPIO lines off, so super drives
  GPIO 17/22 low before restarting it.

Children set `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` and exit when the heartbeat socket hits
EOF, so none outlive super. Super itself runs as a systemd service (`Type=notify`,
`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=1`, `WatchdogSec=3`). It sends `WATCHDOG=1` from its main
loop, so a hung super stops pinging. `ExecStopPost=` forces GPIO 17/22 low. The Pi's
hardware watchdog (`RuntimeWatchdogSec=15`) reboots the board if systemd itself hangs.

## 3. Failure modes
Every log line has the form `<proc>[<pid>] <I|W|E> <event> key=value ...` on stderr, which
systemd stores in journald. Per-frame or per-ping events are never logged individually;
repeats are rate-limited to one line per 10 s with a `count=` field. One representative
line is shown per row.

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| radar | Unplugged or dead → **ultrasonic-only operation** | `cap-radar`: no valid frame for 1 s (UART silent or only bad frames) | Hub → DEG_CLEAR / DEG_IN_ZONE: the ultrasonic warns alone, with the 1 Hz-flash pattern. LCD `RADAR LOST`. The first valid frame restores normal states | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar state=DEG_CLEAR` |
| ultrasonic | Single timeouts (no target, rain, wind) | echo pulse ≥ 25 ms (≥ 4.3 m) | Treated as "nothing in zone". IN_ZONE needs 2 of the last 3 pings, so one dropout doesn't flicker the alert | `cap-sonar[413] I sonar_out_of_range count=812` |
| ultrasonic | Unplugged, dead, or echo stuck high → **radar-only operation** | no echo rising edge within 2 ms of the trigger for 8 pings, or echo high > 60 ms | Hub → DEG_CLEAR / DEG_APPROACHING: the radar warns alone, with the 1 Hz-flash pattern. LCD `SONAR LOST`. Stuck-high needs a power cycle | `cap-sonar[413] W sonar_lost reason=no_echo pings=8` |
| both sensors | Lost together (pod cable cut, pod knocked off) | both of the above | Hub → BLIND: 4 Hz blink and chirps | `fuse-hub[415] E blind lost=radar,sonar` |
| `cap-radar` / `cap-sonar` | The process crashes or hangs (the sensor is fine) | hub: its own staleness timeout (no message for 1 s or 8 ping periods, or EOF); super: SIGCHLD or no heartbeat for 5 s | Hub → the matching DEG state without waiting for a report. Super restarts the process, which reconnects with backoff and reports, and the hub returns to normal states | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar reason=stale silent_ms=1000 state=DEG_CLEAR` |
| `fuse-hub` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; `alert`: no message for 1 s | `alert` → HUB_LOST. Super restarts the hub, which starts in BLIND. Senders reconnect with backoff, through `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the hub's socket is down | `dlby-super[400] E child_exit name=fuse-hub pid=415 signal=SEGV restarts=1 next_ms=100` |
| `alert` | Crash, with the LED or buzzer left on | super: SIGCHLD | Super forces GPIO 17/22 low, then restarts `alert`. The LED is dark meanwhile, which reads "not protected" | `dlby-super[400] I outputs_forced_off gpio=17,22` |
| any child | Hangs without crashing | super: no heartbeat for 5 s (`alert` notices a hung hub in 1 s) | SIGTERM, SIGKILL 500 ms later, then restart. A process stuck in uninterruptible I/O can't be killed; super logs that and keeps waiting | `dlby-super[400] E heartbeat_lost name=store pid=417 silent_ms=5000 action=SIGTERM` |
| `store` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; hub: `EPIPE`, then `ECONNREFUSED` on reconnect | Hub never blocks on `store`: it drops and counts records until reconnect succeeds. Alerts are unaffected. The restarted `store` writes a `GAP` record | `fuse-hub[415] I store_back dropped=37` |
| SD card | Full (`ENOSPC`) | `store`: write returns `ENOSPC` | `store` caps its own log (size in §4) and deletes its oldest segment first. journald is capped with `SystemMaxUse=64M`, so the system log can't fill the card. If the card is still full, `store` keeps only state changes; LCD `LOG FULL`. Alerts are unaffected | `store[417] E enospc_persist mode=state_only free_kb=0` |
| power | Cut mid-write (ignition off) | on next boot, `store` finds a record at the end of the last segment whose length or CRC32 is wrong | Truncate to the last good record and start a new segment. Loss is bounded by `fdatasync` every 1 s and on every state change | `store[417] W torn_tail seg=seg-000123 truncated_bytes=41 last_seq=88213` |
| `dlby-super` | Crash, or hang (no `WATCHDOG=1`) | systemd: main process exits, or no ping for 3 s | systemd kills the whole cgroup, forces the outputs low, and restarts super, which restarts every child. A whole-tree restart is acceptable because it should be rare, and the dark LED reads "not protected", never "clear" | `systemd[1]: dlby.service: Watchdog timeout (limit 3s)!` |

What this table can't promise:
- A process stuck in uninterruptible I/O (D state) needs a reboot to recover.
- A power cut can corrupt the SD card inside its own controller. CRCs detect this but can't
  prevent it (see §5).
- HC-SR04 "stuck high" behavior comes from reports on clone sensors and hasn't been seen on
  ours yet.
- It's unverified whether a released Pi 5 GPIO line keeps its last value. The force-low
  step makes the design independent of the answer.
- The LCD keeps its last text if `status-lcd` dies. A once-per-second tick makes stale text
  visible.
- Single-sensor warnings will raise more false alarms (parked cars, poles), in exchange for
  never going silent while a sensor works.

content.content:
1	# Design document (M2) -- Don't Look Behind You (Jackson Stokes, Gage Boullosa)
2	
3	Hardware and pin map: [docs/HARDWARE.md](docs/HARDWARE.md). Problem statement: [PROBLEM.md](PROBLEM.md).
4	
5	## 1. Architecture
6	
7	![Architecture: processes, kernel components, hardware, and the rate on every link](docs/architecture.svg)
8	
9	Seven processes on the Pi 5, all started and watched by `dlby-super`. Sensor data goes
10	straight from the capture processes to `fuse-hub`, which decides the alert state and
11	forwards a copy of everything to `store`. Unlike a sampler → storage → analysis pipeline,
12	storage is deliberately off the alert path, so a slow SD write can never delay an alert.
13	
14	### Processes
15	| Process | Owner | Role | Scheduling |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `dlby-super` | shared | fork/exec every child, `waitpid`, restart with backoff, kill a child that misses heartbeats for 5 s | SCHED_FIFO 90, asleep almost always |
18	| `cap-radar` | Gage | read `/dev/ttyAMA2`, frame-sync, parse targets, timestamp each frame | SCHED_FIFO 60 |
19	| `cap-sonar` | Gage | trigger GPIO23 on an absolute 60 ms deadline; read kernel-timestamped echo edges on GPIO24 from the gpio character device | SCHED_FIFO 60 |
20	| `fuse-hub` | Jackson | CLEAR → APPROACHING → IN_ZONE → CLEAR state machine; ignores targets that aren't approaching. Keeps its own staleness timeout per sensor (no `radar_msg` for 1 s, no `sonar_msg` for 8 ping periods, or EOF on that connection), so a dead capture process puts it in the matching degraded state without that process having to report anything | SCHED_FIFO 70 |
21	| `alert` | shared | drive the LED (GPIO17) and buzzer (GPIO22); show a fault pattern if `fuse-hub` goes silent | SCHED_FIFO 80 |
22	| `store` | Jackson | append-only log of raw samples and state changes that survives a power cut | SCHED_OTHER, nice +5 |
23	| `status-lcd` | shared | 1602 LCD over I2C1 for bench and demo only. Separate from `alert` so a slow I2C write can't delay the alert | SCHED_OTHER |
24	
25	Kernel components used: the RP1 UART and tty layer (radar), the gpio character device
26	with edge events stamped on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (ultrasonic, LED, buzzer), `i2c-dev` on
27	I2C1 (LCD), and ext4 on the SD card (`store`). The product makes no network calls and has
28	no LAN interface in this milestone.
29	
30	### IPC
31	Every process-to-process link is a Unix domain socket of type `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. Each
32	receiver (`fuse-hub`, `alert`, `store`, `status-lcd`) listens on `/run/dlby/<name>.sock`
33	(directory mode 0700). Senders connect and send with `MSG_NOSIGNAL`. On EOF, `EPIPE`, or a
34	failed connect (`ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the receiver is restarting), they reconnect
35	with backoff (50 ms doubling to 1 s), so any one process can restart without re-wiring the
36	others. `dlby-super` keeps a socketpair to each child for heartbeats only. We chose
37	seqpacket because it keeps message boundaries, a dead peer shows up immediately as
38	EOF/`EPOLLHUP`, and with `SOCK_CLOEXEC` fds can't leak across restarts. Our rates are a few
39	hundred bytes per second, so shared memory's speed isn't needed.
40	
41	### Links and rates
42	| Link | Transport | Payload | Rate | Bandwidth |
43	|---|---|---|---|---|
44	| radar → `cap-radar` | UART 115200 8N1 | frame = 10 B + payload | ~10 Hz | ≤1.3 KB/s (link capacity 11.5 KB/s) |
45	| `cap-sonar` → HC-SR04 | GPIO23 out | 10 µs trigger pulse | 16 Hz | — |
46	| HC-SR04 → `cap-sonar` | GPIO24 edge events | 2 edges per ping | 32 events/s | — |
47	| `cap-radar` → `fuse-hub` | UDS | `radar_msg` ~64 B (timestamp, seq, target count, targets) | 10 Hz | ~640 B/s |
48	| `cap-sonar` → `fuse-hub` | UDS | `sonar_msg` 24 B (timestamp, seq, cm or timeout) | 16 Hz | ~400 B/s |
49	| `fuse-hub` → `alert` | UDS | `alert_msg` 16 B (state, timestamp) | on change + 2 Hz keepalive | <50 B/s |
50	| `fuse-hub` → `store` | UDS | raw messages forwarded, plus state changes | ~26 Hz | ~1.1 KB/s (~4 MB/h, ~190 MB per 48 h soak) |
51	| `fuse-hub` → `status-lcd` | UDS | status snapshot ~64 B | 2 Hz | ~130 B/s |
52	| each child → `dlby-super` | UDS, one per child | heartbeat 8 B | 1 Hz | 8 B/s each |
53	| `status-lcd` → LCD | I2C1 at 100 kHz | 2×16 characters | 2 Hz | — |
54	
55	Two numbers to confirm on hardware:
56	- **Ultrasonic rate.** 16 Hz, not the "~20 Hz" in HARDWARE.md. The HC-SR04 needs at least
57	  60 ms between pings so it doesn't hear the previous ping's echo, and the bench sketch
58	  already uses 60 ms.
59	- **Radar payload size** is an estimate until the LD2451 frame format is checked against
60	  the datasheet and real captures.
61	
62	### Fusion states and driver signals
63	While both sensors are healthy, neither alone raises an alert: APPROACHING needs a radar
64	track, and IN_ZONE needs the ultrasonic to confirm it. If one sensor is lost, the survivor
65	still warns, but in a pattern the driver can tell apart. `fuse-hub` starts in BLIND. It
66	moves to the normal states once both sensors report, or to the matching DEG state if one
67	reports and the other stays silent past its loss timeout (radar 1 s, ultrasonic 8 pings).
68	
69	The rule for the driver:
70	- **Solid:** warning, both sensors healthy.
71	- **1 Hz flash:** warning from one sensor only (unconfirmed).
72	- **Short blink every 2 s:** armed. A single blink means both sensors are healthy; a
73	  double blink means one sensor is lost.
74	- **4 Hz blink:** not protected.
75	- **Dark:** system not running.
76	
77	The LED is never dark while the system is working, so dark can't be mistaken for "clear".
78	The buzzer is an active (fixed-tone) part, so its patterns are timing only.
79	
80	| State | Meaning | LED | Buzzer | LCD (bench) |
81	|---|---|---|---|---|
82	| CLEAR | both healthy, nothing near | single 50 ms blink every 2 s | silent | `ARMED` |
83	| APPROACHING | both healthy, radar track approaching | solid | silent | `APPROACH 23m` |
84	| IN_ZONE | both healthy, ultrasonic confirms the track | solid | 4 Hz beeps | `IN ZONE` |
85	| DEG_CLEAR | one sensor lost, survivor sees nothing | double blink every 2 s | one chirp on entry | `RADAR LOST` / `SONAR LOST` |
86	| DEG_APPROACHING | ultrasonic lost, radar track approaching | 1 Hz flash | silent | `SONAR LOST APPR` |
87	| DEG_IN_ZONE | radar lost, something at 0.2–4 m (unconfirmed) | 1 Hz flash | 1 Hz beeps | `RADAR LOST ZONE` |
88	| BLIND | both sensors lost, or hub just started | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, again every 30 s | `NO SENSORS` |
89	| HUB_LOST (`alert`'s own state) | no message from `fuse-hub` for 1 s | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, again every 30 s | `HUB DOWN` |
90	| no process running | supervisor restart, boot, power off | dark | silent | stale text |
91	
92	BLIND and HUB_LOST share a pattern on purpose. Both mean "not protected", and the LCD
93	tells them apart on the bench.
94	
95	## 2. Mechanism mapping
96	
97	### C: SCHED_FIFO on the alert chain (`cap-radar`, `cap-sonar`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`)
98	**Not the justification: range accuracy.** The kernel timestamps echo edges in the GPIO
99	interrupt path, so the measured range, (t_fall − t_rise) × 343 m/s ÷ 2, doesn't depend on
100	when `cap-sonar` gets to run. The trigger time doesn't matter either, because the echo's
101	rising edge is the reference. Scheduling could only cost range data if the kernel's
102	16-event edge buffer overflowed, which takes more than about 250 ms of starvation at
103	32 events/s.
104	
105	**The justification:**
106	1. **Alert latency under load.** A sensor reading reaches the buzzer through three
107	   wakeups: capture, `fuse-hub`, `alert`. Under the default scheduler, with `store`
108	   flushing to the SD card and other load on the CPU, each wakeup can slip by milliseconds
109	   to tens of milliseconds. At a 30 km/h closing speed (8.3 m/s), 50 ms is about 0.4 m of
110	   cyclist travel inside a 4 m zone. The whole chain runs SCHED_FIFO, with priority rising
111	   downstream (capture 60 < `fuse-hub` 70 < `alert` 80) so each stage runs as soon as its
112	   input arrives.
113	2. **Regular trigger period.** A late wakeup stretches the gap between pings, which adds
114	   directly to the worst-case detection delay. Periodic wakeups use absolute deadlines
115	   (`clock_nanosleep` with `TIMER_ABSTIME`) so lateness doesn't accumulate.
116	3. **Radar timestamps.** UART bytes are buffered by the kernel and timestamped in user
117	   space when read, so radar timestamps do shift with scheduling delay. The fusion check
118	   that the ultrasonic hit matches the radar's last track depends on them.
119	
120	**Keeping C safe:** every real-time process calls `mlockall`. The kernel's real-time
121	throttle (`sched_rt_runtime_us`, 950 ms per second) stays at its default, so a real-time
122	child stuck in a loop can't starve the system. `dlby-super` has the highest priority and
123	almost always sleeps, so it can still detect and kill a stuck child.
124	
125	### D: crash-consistent storage
126	TODO
127	
128	### E: multi-process architecture with a supervisor
129	**Justification:** an outdoor sensor pod will fail in ordinary use (cable knocked loose,
130	water, a locked-up ultrasonic). The driver must keep getting warnings from whatever still
131	works, and must never read "LED dark" as "no cyclist". One process per job means one
132	failure costs one component, and a supervisor turns every failure into a visible state.
133	
134	`dlby-super`:
135	- **Starts** every child in order (`store`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`, `status-lcd`, `cap-radar`,
136	  `cap-sonar`). Each gets a heartbeat socketpair and nothing else, since every fd is
137	  `O_CLOEXEC`/`SOCK_CLOEXEC`.
138	- **Detects crashes** with SIGCHLD through a `signalfd`, then reaps with `waitpid(WNOHANG)`.
139	- **Detects hangs.** Each child sends a heartbeat every 1 s from its main event loop, never
140	  from a side thread, so a stuck loop stops the heartbeat. After 5 s of silence super sends
141	  SIGTERM, and SIGKILL 500 ms later. Children get 10 s after start to send their first
142	  heartbeat (CLAUDE.md allows up to 60 s).
143	- **Restarts** with backoff from 100 ms doubling to 30 s, reset after 60 s healthy. It never
144	  gives up on a sensor, since it may be re-plugged.
145	- **Reads exit codes:** 0 means asked to stop (no restart). 69 `EX_UNAVAILABLE` (device
146	  missing) and 70 `EX_SOFTWARE` (internal error) mean restart with backoff. 78 `EX_CONFIG`
147	  means don't restart, and log it.
148	- **Clears stuck outputs.** A killed `alert` can't turn its GPIO lines off, so super drives
149	  GPIO 17/22 low before restarting it.
150	
151	Children set `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` and exit when the heartbeat socket hits
152	EOF, so none outlive super. Super itself runs as a systemd service (`Type=notify`,
153	`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=1`, `WatchdogSec=3`). It sends `WATCHDOG=1` from its main
154	loop, so a hung super stops pinging. `ExecStopPost=` forces GPIO 17/22 low. The Pi's
155	hardware watchdog (`RuntimeWatchdogSec=15`) reboots the board if systemd itself hangs.
156	
157	## 3. Failure modes
158	Every log line has the form `<proc>[<pid>] <I|W|E> <event> key=value ...` on stderr, which
159	systemd stores in journald. Per-frame or per-ping events are never logged individually;
160	repeats are rate-limited to one line per 10 s with a `count=` field. One representative
161	line is shown per row.
162	
163	| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
164	|---|---|---|---|---|
165	| radar | Unplugged or dead → **ultrasonic-only operation** | `cap-radar`: no valid frame for 1 s (UART silent or only bad frames) | Hub → DEG_CLEAR / DEG_IN_ZONE: the ultrasonic warns alone, with the 1 Hz-flash pattern. LCD `RADAR LOST`. The first valid frame restores normal states | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar state=DEG_CLEAR` |
166	| ultrasonic | Single timeouts (no target, rain, wind) | echo pulse ≥ 25 ms (≥ 4.3 m) | Treated as "nothing in zone". IN_ZONE needs 2 of the last 3 pings, so one dropout doesn't flicker the alert | `cap-sonar[413] I sonar_out_of_range count=812` |
167	| ultrasonic | Unplugged, dead, or echo stuck high → **radar-only operation** | no echo rising edge within 2 ms of the trigger for 8 pings, or echo high > 60 ms | Hub → DEG_CLEAR / DEG_APPROACHING: the radar warns alone, with the 1 Hz-flash pattern. LCD `SONAR LOST`. Stuck-high needs a power cycle | `cap-sonar[413] W sonar_lost reason=no_echo pings=8` |
168	| both sensors | Lost together (pod cable cut, pod knocked off) | both of the above | Hub → BLIND: 4 Hz blink and chirps | `fuse-hub[415] E blind lost=radar,sonar` |
169	| `cap-radar` / `cap-sonar` | The process crashes or hangs (the sensor is fine) | hub: its own staleness timeout (no message for 1 s or 8 ping periods, or EOF); super: SIGCHLD or no heartbeat for 5 s | Hub → the matching DEG state without waiting for a report. Super restarts the process, which reconnects with backoff and reports, and the hub returns to normal states | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar reason=stale silent_ms=1000 state=DEG_CLEAR` |
170	| `fuse-hub` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; `alert`: no message for 1 s | `alert` → HUB_LOST. Super restarts the hub, which starts in BLIND. Senders reconnect with backoff, through `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the hub's socket is down | `dlby-super[400] E child_exit name=fuse-hub pid=415 signal=SEGV restarts=1 next_ms=100` |

# Design document (M2) -- Don't Look Behind You (Jackson Stokes, Gage Boullosa)

Hardware and pin map: [docs/HARDWARE.md](docs/HARDWARE.md). Problem statement: [PROBLEM.md](PROBLEM.md).

## 1. Architecture

![Architecture: processes, kernel components, hardware, and the rate on every link](docs/architecture.svg)

Seven processes on the Pi 5, all started and watched by `dlby-super`. Sensor data goes
straight from the capture processes to `fuse-hub`, which decides the alert state and
forwards a copy of everything to `store`. Unlike a sampler → storage → analysis pipeline,
storage is deliberately off the alert path, so a slow SD write can never delay an alert.

### Processes
| Process | Owner | Role | Scheduling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dlby-super` | shared | fork/exec every child, `waitpid`, restart with backoff, kill a child that misses heartbeats for 5 s | SCHED_FIFO 90, asleep almost always |
| `cap-radar` | Gage | read `/dev/ttyAMA2`, frame-sync, parse targets, timestamp each frame | SCHED_FIFO 60 |
| `cap-sonar` | Gage | trigger GPIO23 on an absolute 60 ms deadline; read kernel-timestamped echo edges on GPIO24 from the gpio character device | SCHED_FIFO 60 |
| `fuse-hub` | Jackson | CLEAR → APPROACHING → IN_ZONE → CLEAR state machine; ignores targets that aren't approaching. Keeps its own staleness timeout per sensor (no `radar_msg` for 1 s, no `sonar_msg` for 8 ping periods, or EOF on that connection), so a dead capture process puts it in the matching degraded state without that process having to report anything | SCHED_FIFO 70 |
| `alert` | shared | drive the LED (GPIO17) and buzzer (GPIO22); show a fault pattern if `fuse-hub` goes silent | SCHED_FIFO 80 |
| `store` | Jackson | append-only log of raw samples and state changes that survives a power cut | SCHED_OTHER, nice +5 |
| `status-lcd` | shared | 1602 LCD over I2C1 for bench and demo only. Separate from `alert` so a slow I2C write can't delay the alert | SCHED_OTHER |

Kernel components used: the RP1 UART and tty layer (radar), the gpio character device
with edge events stamped on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` (ultrasonic, LED, buzzer), `i2c-dev` on
I2C1 (LCD), and ext4 on the SD card (`store`). The product makes no network calls and has
no LAN interface in this milestone.

### IPC
Every process-to-process link is a Unix domain socket of type `SOCK_SEQPACKET`. Each
receiver (`fuse-hub`, `alert`, `store`, `status-lcd`) listens on `/run/dlby/<name>.sock`
(directory mode 0700). Senders connect and send with `MSG_NOSIGNAL`. On EOF, `EPIPE`, or a
failed connect (`ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the receiver is restarting), they reconnect
with backoff (50 ms doubling to 1 s), so any one process can restart without re-wiring the
others. `dlby-super` keeps a socketpair to each child for heartbeats only. We chose
seqpacket because it keeps message boundaries, a dead peer shows up immediately as
EOF/`EPOLLHUP`, and with `SOCK_CLOEXEC` fds can't leak across restarts. Our rates are a few
hundred bytes per second, so shared memory's speed isn't needed.

### Links and rates
| Link | Transport | Payload | Rate | Bandwidth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| radar → `cap-radar` | UART 115200 8N1 | frame = 10 B + payload | ~10 Hz | ≤1.3 KB/s (link capacity 11.5 KB/s) |
| `cap-sonar` → HC-SR04 | GPIO23 out | 10 µs trigger pulse | 16 Hz | — |
| HC-SR04 → `cap-sonar` | GPIO24 edge events | 2 edges per ping | 32 events/s | — |
| `cap-radar` → `fuse-hub` | UDS | `radar_msg` ~64 B (timestamp, seq, target count, targets) | 10 Hz | ~640 B/s |
| `cap-sonar` → `fuse-hub` | UDS | `sonar_msg` 24 B (timestamp, seq, cm or timeout) | 16 Hz | ~400 B/s |
| `fuse-hub` → `alert` | UDS | `alert_msg` 16 B (state, timestamp) | on change + 2 Hz keepalive | <50 B/s |
| `fuse-hub` → `store` | UDS | raw messages forwarded, plus state changes | ~26 Hz | ~1.1 KB/s (~4 MB/h, ~190 MB per 48 h soak) |
| `fuse-hub` → `status-lcd` | UDS | status snapshot ~64 B | 2 Hz | ~130 B/s |
| each child → `dlby-super` | UDS, one per child | heartbeat 8 B | 1 Hz | 8 B/s each |
| `status-lcd` → LCD | I2C1 at 100 kHz | 2×16 characters | 2 Hz | — |

Two numbers to confirm on hardware:
- **Ultrasonic rate.** 16 Hz, not the "~20 Hz" in HARDWARE.md. The HC-SR04 needs at least
  60 ms between pings so it doesn't hear the previous ping's echo, and the bench sketch
  already uses 60 ms.
- **Radar payload size** is an estimate until the LD2451 frame format is checked against
  the datasheet and real captures.

### Fusion states and driver signals
While both sensors are healthy, neither alone raises an alert: APPROACHING needs a radar
track, and IN_ZONE needs the ultrasonic to confirm it. If one sensor is lost, the survivor
still warns, but in a pattern the driver can tell apart. `fuse-hub` starts in BLIND. It
moves to the normal states once both sensors report, or to the matching DEG state if one
reports and the other stays silent past its loss timeout (radar 1 s, ultrasonic 8 pings).

The rule for the driver:
- **Solid:** warning, both sensors healthy.
- **1 Hz flash:** warning from one sensor only (unconfirmed).
- **Short blink every 2 s:** armed. A single blink means both sensors are healthy; a
  double blink means one sensor is lost.
- **4 Hz blink:** not protected.
- **Dark:** system not running.

The LED is never dark while the system is working, so dark can't be mistaken for "clear".
The buzzer is an active (fixed-tone) part, so its patterns are timing only.

| State | Meaning | LED | Buzzer | LCD (bench) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLEAR | both healthy, nothing near | single 50 ms blink every 2 s | silent | `ARMED` |
| APPROACHING | both healthy, radar track approaching | solid | silent | `APPROACH 23m` |
| IN_ZONE | both healthy, ultrasonic confirms the track | solid | 4 Hz beeps | `IN ZONE` |
| DEG_CLEAR | one sensor lost, survivor sees nothing | double blink every 2 s | one chirp on entry | `RADAR LOST` / `SONAR LOST` |
| DEG_APPROACHING | ultrasonic lost, radar track approaching | 1 Hz flash | silent | `SONAR LOST APPR` |
| DEG_IN_ZONE | radar lost, something at 0.2–4 m (unconfirmed) | 1 Hz flash | 1 Hz beeps | `RADAR LOST ZONE` |
| BLIND | both sensors lost, or hub just started | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, again every 30 s | `NO SENSORS` |
| HUB_LOST (`alert`'s own state) | no message from `fuse-hub` for 1 s | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, again every 30 s | `HUB DOWN` |
| no process running | supervisor restart, boot, power off | dark | silent | stale text |

BLIND and HUB_LOST share a pattern on purpose. Both mean "not protected", and the LCD
tells them apart on the bench.

## 2. Mechanism mapping

### C: SCHED_FIFO on the alert chain (`cap-radar`, `cap-sonar`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`)
**Not the justification: range accuracy.** The kernel timestamps echo edges in the GPIO
interrupt path, so the measured range, (t_fall − t_rise) × 343 m/s ÷ 2, doesn't depend on
when `cap-sonar` gets to run. The trigger time doesn't matter either, because the echo's
rising edge is the reference. Scheduling could only cost range data if the kernel's
16-event edge buffer overflowed, which takes more than about 250 ms of starvation at
32 events/s.

**The justification:**
1. **Alert latency under load.** A sensor reading reaches the buzzer through three
   wakeups: capture, `fuse-hub`, `alert`. Under the default scheduler, with `store`
   flushing to the SD card and other load on the CPU, each wakeup can slip by milliseconds
   to tens of milliseconds. At a 30 km/h closing speed (8.3 m/s), 50 ms is about 0.4 m of
   cyclist travel inside a 4 m zone. The whole chain runs SCHED_FIFO, with priority rising
   downstream (capture 60 < `fuse-hub` 70 < `alert` 80) so each stage runs as soon as its
   input arrives.
2. **Regular trigger period.** A late wakeup stretches the gap between pings, which adds
   directly to the worst-case detection delay. Periodic wakeups use absolute deadlines
   (`clock_nanosleep` with `TIMER_ABSTIME`) so lateness doesn't accumulate.
3. **Radar timestamps.** UART bytes are buffered by the kernel and timestamped in user
   space when read, so radar timestamps do shift with scheduling delay. The fusion check
   that the ultrasonic hit matches the radar's last track depends on them.

**Keeping C safe:** every real-time process calls `mlockall`. The kernel's real-time
throttle (`sched_rt_runtime_us`, 950 ms per second) stays at its default, so a real-time
child stuck in a loop can't starve the system. `dlby-super` has the highest priority and
almost always sleeps, so it can still detect and kill a stuck child.

### D: crash-consistent storage
TODO

### E: multi-process architecture with a supervisor
**Justification:** an outdoor sensor pod will fail in ordinary use (cable knocked loose,
water, a locked-up ultrasonic). The driver must keep getting warnings from whatever still
works, and must never read "LED dark" as "no cyclist". One process per job means one
failure costs one component, and a supervisor turns every failure into a visible state.

`dlby-super`:
- **Starts** every child in order (`store`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`, `status-lcd`, `cap-radar`,
  `cap-sonar`). Each gets a heartbeat socketpair and nothing else, since every fd is
  `O_CLOEXEC`/`SOCK_CLOEXEC`.
- **Detects crashes** with SIGCHLD through a `signalfd`, then reaps with `waitpid(WNOHANG)`.
- **Detects hangs.** Each child sends a heartbeat every 1 s from its main event loop, never
  from a side thread, so a stuck loop stops the heartbeat. After 5 s of silence super sends
  SIGTERM, and SIGKILL 500 ms later. Children get 10 s after start to send their first
  heartbeat (CLAUDE.md allows up to 60 s).
- **Restarts** with backoff from 100 ms doubling to 30 s, reset after 60 s healthy. It never
  gives up on a sensor, since it may be re-plugged.
- **Reads exit codes:** 0 means asked to stop (no restart). 69 `EX_UNAVAILABLE` (device
  missing) and 70 `EX_SOFTWARE` (internal error) mean restart with backoff. 78 `EX_CONFIG`
  means don't restart, and log it.
- **Clears stuck outputs.** A killed `alert` can't turn its GPIO lines off, so super drives
  GPIO 17/22 low before restarting it.

Children set `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` and exit when the heartbeat socket hits
EOF, so none outlive super. Super itself runs as a systemd service (`Type=notify`,
`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=1`, `WatchdogSec=3`). It sends `WATCHDOG=1` from its main
loop, so a hung super stops pinging. `ExecStopPost=` forces GPIO 17/22 low. The Pi's
hardware watchdog (`RuntimeWatchdogSec=15`) reboots the board if systemd itself hangs.

## 3. Failure modes
Every log line has the form `<proc>[<pid>] <I|W|E> <event> key=value ...` on stderr, which
systemd stores in journald. Per-frame or per-ping events are never logged individually;
repeats are rate-limited to one line per 10 s with a `count=` field. One representative
line is shown per row.

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| radar | Unplugged or dead → **ultrasonic-only operation** | `cap-radar`: no valid frame for 1 s (UART silent or only bad frames) | Hub → DEG_CLEAR / DEG_IN_ZONE: the ultrasonic warns alone, with the 1 Hz-flash pattern. LCD `RADAR LOST`. The first valid frame restores normal states | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar state=DEG_CLEAR` |
| ultrasonic | Single timeouts (no target, rain, wind) | echo pulse ≥ 25 ms (≥ 4.3 m) | Treated as "nothing in zone". IN_ZONE needs 2 of the last 3 pings, so one dropout doesn't flicker the alert | `cap-sonar[413] I sonar_out_of_range count=812` |
| ultrasonic | Unplugged, dead, or echo stuck high → **radar-only operation** | no echo rising edge within 2 ms of the trigger for 8 pings, or echo high > 60 ms | Hub → DEG_CLEAR / DEG_APPROACHING: the radar warns alone, with the 1 Hz-flash pattern. LCD `SONAR LOST`. Stuck-high needs a power cycle | `cap-sonar[413] W sonar_lost reason=no_echo pings=8` |
| both sensors | Lost together (pod cable cut, pod knocked off) | both of the above | Hub → BLIND: 4 Hz blink and chirps | `fuse-hub[415] E blind lost=radar,sonar` |
| `cap-radar` / `cap-sonar` | The process crashes or hangs (the sensor is fine) | hub: its own staleness timeout (no message for 1 s or 8 ping periods, or EOF); super: SIGCHLD or no heartbeat for 5 s | Hub → the matching DEG state without waiting for a report. Super restarts the process, which reconnects with backoff and reports, and the hub returns to normal states | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar reason=stale silent_ms=1000 state=DEG_CLEAR` |
| `fuse-hub` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; `alert`: no message for 1 s | `alert` → HUB_LOST. Super restarts the hub, which starts in BLIND. Senders reconnect with backoff, through `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the hub's socket is down | `dlby-super[400] E child_exit name=fuse-hub pid=415 signal=SEGV restarts=1 next_ms=100` |
| `alert` | Crash, with the LED or buzzer left on | super: SIGCHLD | Super forces GPIO 17/22 low, then restarts `alert`. The LED is dark meanwhile, which reads "not protected" | `dlby-super[400] I outputs_forced_off gpio=17,22` |
| any child | Hangs without crashing | super: no heartbeat for 5 s (`alert` notices a hung hub in 1 s) | SIGTERM, SIGKILL 500 ms later, then restart. A process stuck in uninterruptible I/O can't be killed; super logs that and keeps waiting | `dlby-super[400] E heartbeat_lost name=store pid=417 silent_ms=5000 action=SIGTERM` |
| `store` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; hub: `EPIPE`, then `ECONNREFUSED` on reconnect | Hub never blocks on `store`: it drops and counts records until reconnect succeeds. Alerts are unaffected. The restarted `store` writes a `GAP` record | `fuse-hub[415] I store_back dropped=37` |
| SD card | Full (`ENOSPC`) | `store`: write returns `ENOSPC` | `store` caps its own log (size in §4) and deletes its oldest segment first. journald is capped with `SystemMaxUse=64M`, so the system log can't fill the card. If the card is still full, `store` keeps only state changes; LCD `LOG FULL`. Alerts are unaffected | `store[417] E enospc_persist mode=state_only free_kb=0` |
| power | Cut mid-write (ignition off) | on next boot, `store` finds a record at the end of the last segment whose length or CRC32 is wrong | Truncate to the last good record and start a new segment. Loss is bounded by `fdatasync` every 1 s and on every state change | `store[417] W torn_tail seg=seg-000123 truncated_bytes=41 last_seq=88213` |
| `dlby-super` | Crash, or hang (no `WATCHDOG=1`) | systemd: main process exits, or no ping for 3 s | systemd kills the whole cgroup, forces the outputs low, and restarts super, which restarts every child. A whole-tree restart is acceptable because it should be rare, and the dark LED reads "not protected", never "clear" | `systemd[1]: dlby.service: Watchdog timeout (limit 3s)!` |

What this table can't promise:

- A power cut can corrupt the SD card inside its own controller. CRCs detect this but can't

- HC-SR04 "stuck high" behavior comes from reports on clone sensors and hasn't been seen on

| CLEAR | both healthy, nothing near | single 50 ms blink / 2 s | silent |
| APPROACHING | both healthy, radar track approaching | solid | silent |
| IN_ZONE | both healthy, ultrasonic confirms the track | solid | 4 Hz beeps |
| DEG_CLEAR | one sensor lost, survivor sees nothing | double blink / 2 s | one chirp on entry |
| DEG_APPROACHING | ultrasonic lost, radar track approaching | 1 Hz flash | silent |

## 2. Mechanism mapping

### C: SCHED_FIFO on the alert chain (`cap-radar`, `cap-sonar`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`)
**Not the reason: range accuracy.** The kernel timestamps echo edges in the GPIO interrupt
path, so range = (t_fall − t_rise) × 343 m/s ÷ 2 doesn't depend on when `cap-sonar` runs.
Losing range data would take >250 ms of starvation to overflow the 16-event edge buffer.

**The reasons:**
1. **Alert latency under load.** A reading reaches the buzzer through three wakeups
   (capture, `fuse-hub`, `alert`). Under the default scheduler, with `store` flushing to
   the SD card, each can slip by milliseconds to tens of milliseconds. At 30 km/h closing
   speed, 50 ms is 0.4 m of a 4 m zone. Priority rises downstream (60 < 70 < 80) so each
   stage runs as soon as its input arrives.
2. **Regular trigger period.** A late wakeup stretches the gap between pings and adds to
   worst-case detection delay. Absolute deadlines (`clock_nanosleep`, `TIMER_ABSTIME`)
   stop lateness accumulating.
3. **Radar timestamps** are taken in user space on `read`, so they shift with scheduling
   delay, and fusion compares them against ultrasonic hits.

**Safety:** every real-time process calls `mlockall`. The RT throttle
(`sched_rt_runtime_us` = 950 ms/s) stays on, so a spinning child can't starve the system,
and `dlby-super` at priority 90 can still kill it.

### E: multi-process architecture with a supervisor
**Reason:** an outdoor sensor pod will fail in ordinary use (loose cable, water, a
locked-up ultrasonic). The driver must keep getting warnings from whatever still works and
must never read "LED dark" as "no cyclist". One process per job means one failure costs one
component, and the supervisor turns every failure into a visible state.

`dlby-super` starts the children in order (`store`, `fuse-hub`, `alert`, `status-lcd`,
`cap-radar`, `cap-sonar`). Each child inherits only its heartbeat socketpair, since every
fd is close-on-exec.
- **Crash:** SIGCHLD via `signalfd`, reaped with `waitpid(WNOHANG)`.
- **Hang:** each child sends a heartbeat every 1 s from its main event loop, never a side
  thread, so a stuck loop goes quiet. After 5 s of silence: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 500 ms
  later. The first heartbeat is due within 10 s of start (CLAUDE.md allows 60 s).
- **Restart:** backoff 100 ms doubling to 30 s, reset after 60 s healthy; it never gives up
  on a sensor. Exit codes: 0 = stopped on request, no restart; 69 `EX_UNAVAILABLE` and
  70 `EX_SOFTWARE` = restart; 78 `EX_CONFIG` = log and don't restart.
- **Stuck outputs:** a killed `alert` can't release its GPIO lines safely, so super drives
  GPIO 17/22 low before restarting it.

Children set `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` and exit on heartbeat-socket EOF, so none outlive super.
Super runs under systemd (`Type=notify`, `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=1`,
`WatchdogSec=3`) and sends `WATCHDOG=1` from its main loop, so a hung super stops pinging.
`ExecStopPost=` forces GPIO 17/22 low. The Pi's hardware watchdog
(`RuntimeWatchdogSec=15`) reboots the board if systemd itself hangs.

## 3. Failure modes
Log lines have the form `<proc>[<pid>] <I|W|E> <event> key=value ...` on stderr, stored by
journald. Per-frame and per-ping events are never logged; repeats are limited to one line
per 10 s with a `count=` field.

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| radar | Unplugged or dead → ultrasonic-only | `cap-radar`: no valid frame for 1 s | Hub → DEG states; ultrasonic warns alone. Recovers on the first valid frame | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar state=DEG_CLEAR` |
| ultrasonic | Single timeouts (no target, rain, wind) | echo ≥ 25 ms (≥ 4.3 m) | Treated as "nothing in zone"; IN_ZONE needs 2 of the last 3 pings | `cap-sonar[413] I sonar_out_of_range count=812` |
| ultrasonic | Unplugged, dead, or echo stuck high → radar-only | no echo edge within 2 ms for 8 pings, or echo high > 60 ms | Hub → DEG states; radar warns alone. Stuck-high needs a power cycle | `cap-sonar[413] W sonar_lost reason=no_echo pings=8` |
| both sensors | Lost together (pod cable cut) | both of the above | Hub → BLIND | `fuse-hub[415] E blind lost=radar,sonar` |
| `cap-radar`, `cap-sonar` | Process crashes or hangs | hub: staleness timeout or EOF; super: SIGCHLD or heartbeat | Hub → DEG at once, without a report. Super restarts the process; it reconnects and the hub returns to normal | `fuse-hub[415] W degraded lost=radar reason=stale silent_ms=1000` |
| `fuse-hub` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; `alert`: silent 1 s | `alert` → HUB_LOST. Restarted hub starts in BLIND; senders retry through `ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` | `dlby-super[400] E child_exit name=fuse-hub pid=415 signal=SEGV next_ms=100` |
| `alert` | Crash with LED or buzzer left on | super: SIGCHLD | Super forces GPIO 17/22 low, then restarts it; the LED is dark (not protected) meanwhile | `dlby-super[400] I outputs_forced_off gpio=17,22` |
| any child | Hangs without crashing | super: no heartbeat for 5 s | SIGTERM, SIGKILL 500 ms later, restart | `dlby-super[400] E heartbeat_lost name=store pid=417 action=SIGTERM` |
| `store` | Crash | super: SIGCHLD; hub: `EPIPE` | Hub drops and counts records until it reconnects; alerts unaffected; `store` writes a `GAP` record | `fuse-hub[415] I store_back dropped=37` |
| SD card | Full (`ENOSPC`) | `store`: write fails | `store` deletes its oldest segment (its cap is in §4). journald capped by `SystemMaxUse=64M`. Still full: keep state changes only | `store[417] E enospc_persist mode=state_only` |
| power | Cut mid-write | next boot: bad length or CRC32 at the log's tail | Truncate to the last good record. Loss ≤ 1 s (`fdatasync` every 1 s and on state change) | `store[417] W torn_tail truncated_bytes=41 last_seq=88213` |
| `dlby-super` | Crash, or hang (no `WATCHDOG=1`) | systemd: exit, or no ping for 3 s | systemd kills the cgroup, forces outputs low, restarts the whole tree. Rare, and a dark LED reads "not protected", never "clear" | `systemd[1]: dlby.service: Watchdog timeout (limit 3s)!` |

Limits:
- A process stuck in uninterruptible I/O (D state) can't be killed; only a reboot recovers.
- A power cut can corrupt the SD card's controller; CRCs detect damage but can't prevent it.
- HC-SR04 stuck-high comes from clone-sensor reports, not yet seen on ours.
- Whether a released Pi 5 GPIO line holds its value is unverified; forcing it low sidesteps this.
- Single-sensor warnings add false alarms (parked cars, poles) to avoid going silent.

on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), `i2c-dev`, and ext4 on the SD card. No network calls, no LAN interface.

**IPC.** Every process-to-process link is a Unix domain socket (UDS) of type
`SOCK_SEQPACKET`. Each receiver (`fuse-hub`, `alert`, `store`, `status-lcd`) listens on
`/run/dlby/<name>.sock` (directory mode 0700). Senders use `MSG_NOSIGNAL`. On EOF, `EPIPE`,
or a failed connect (`ECONNREFUSED`/`ENOENT` while the receiver is restarting), they
reconnect with backoff (50 ms doubling to 1 s), so any process can restart without
re-wiring the others. `dlby-super` keeps a socketpair to each child for heartbeats only.
Seqpacket keeps message boundaries and reports a dead peer at once as EOF/`EPOLLHUP`, and
`SOCK_CLOEXEC` stops fds leaking across restarts. At a few hundred B/s, shared memory's
speed isn't needed.

input.old_string:
For the driver: solid = warning, both sensors healthy. 1 Hz flash = warning from one sensor
only (unconfirmed). Short blink every 2 s = armed (single blink = both sensors healthy,
double blink = one sensor lost). 4 Hz blink = not protected. Dark = system not running.
The buzzer is an active (fixed-tone) part, so patterns are timing only. The bench LCD shows
the state and, in DEG states, which sensor is lost.

| State | Meaning | LED | Buzzer |
|---|---|---|---|
| CLEAR | both healthy, nothing near | single 50 ms blink / 2 s | silent |
| APPROACHING | both healthy, radar track approaching | solid | silent |
| IN_ZONE | both healthy, ultrasonic confirms the track | solid | 4 Hz beeps |
| DEG_CLEAR | one sensor lost, survivor sees nothing | double blink / 2 s | one chirp on entry |
| DEG_APPROACHING | ultrasonic lost, radar track approaching | 1 Hz flash | silent |
| DEG_IN_ZONE | radar lost, something at 0.2–4 m | 1 Hz flash | 1 Hz beeps |
| BLIND | both sensors lost, or hub just started | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, every 30 s |
| HUB_LOST (`alert`'s own) | nothing from `fuse-hub` for 1 s | 4 Hz blink | two chirps on entry, every 30 s |
| nothing running | supervisor restart, boot, power off | dark | silent |

BLIND and HUB_LOST share a pattern on purpose: both mean "not protected".

Children set `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` and exit on heartbeat-socket EOF, so none outlive super.
Super runs under systemd (`Type=notify`, `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=1`,

(`RuntimeWatchdogSec=15`) reboots the board if systemd itself hangs.

- **Narrowing the failure-table log column:** about 0.1 pages, by dropping the `[pid]` from each example line, since the format line already says it's there.

# Problem memo -- Don't Look Behind You (Jackson Stokes, Gage Boullosa)

## The user 
A person or place, named or nameable. Who will this sit next to? 

A driver in Fort Collins. The device mounts on the car: a sensor pod outside on the right rear quarter, cabled through the door seal to a Raspberry Pi 5 inside the cabin, with an alert LED on the dash or right A-pillar.

## The problem 
What goes wrong, how often, and what it costs (money, worry, ruined batches, missed warnings). Observable, not hypothetical. 

A driver turning right doesn't see a cyclist coming up in the right-side blind spot and turns across them (the "right-hook"). In Fort Collins, cyclists get hit by cars this way, costing hospital bills, legal fees, and insurance claims. Factory blind-spot monitoring is missing on older cars and is tuned to detect cars, not cyclists.

## Why a device 
The 3 a.m. test: why must something be physically present and always awake? Why doesn't a phone app already solve this? 

The sensors must be physically mounted outside the car, aimed at the blind spot, and awake the whole time the car is moving; neither sensor works through glass. A phone in the cabin has no rear-facing radar or ranging sensor and can't see the blind spot.

## The sensors 
Which two (or more), and how they COOPERATE (fused, correlated, or one pipeline) rather than merely coexist. 

- HLK-LD2451 24GHz radar (UART, ~10Hz), facing rearward along the right side: range, speed, and approach direction at roughly 5-50m.
- HC-SR04 ultrasonic (~20Hz; JSN-SR04T for the outdoor build), facing sideways: confirms something is in the 0.2-4m blind-spot zone.

They are fused by a state machine that hands off between the two range bands: CLEAR -> APPROACHING (radar sees an approaching target) -> IN_ZONE (ultrasonic detects something consistent with the radar's last track) -> CLEAR. While both sensors are healthy, neither alone raises the alert; if one is lost, the survivor still warns, using a distinct degraded pattern.

## The mechanisms 
First guess at two items from the Section 3.2 menu, one sentence of justification each. Allowed to change by the design doc. 

C. Real-time scheduling (SCHED_FIFO/SCHED_RR) for a latency-critical path. 

A warning reaches the driver through three processes (sensor capture, fusion, alert), and under CPU or disk load each hand-off can be delayed by tens of milliseconds, so the whole alert chain needs SCHED_FIFO to keep that delay bounded.

E. A multi-process architecture: sensors isolated in separate processes, a hub aggregating over IPC (shared memory, message queues, or Unix domain sockets), a supervisor that survives any child dying.

One process per sensor plus a fusion hub under a supervisor, so an unplugged or crashed sensor degrades the system instead of taking it down.

(D, the storage layer, is a candidate third: ignition-off cuts power mid-write.)

## The risk 
The single thing most likely to sink this project. Name it now; it is cheaper to meet in Week 5 than in Week 14.

The radar may not detect cyclists far enough out. Its ~100m spec is for cars; a cyclist is a much smaller target. Go/no-go test: a cyclist passes the parked car, logging first-detect range over 5+ passes, with a target of at least 20m.
